core_invariant: A restart may lose availability; it must not restore spendable authorization, erase a known revocation or terminal state, or convert uncertainty into permission.

attack_classes.threat: Two processes extend one authorization state concurrently.
attack_classes.control: Signed exclusive writer lease; every commit rereads and verifies ownership before creating a generation.
attack_classes.residual_nonclaim: This is not a distributed lease or consensus protocol.

attack_classes.threat: A stale lock is broken while an older writer can still mutate state.
attack_classes.control: Lease expiry plus exact externally retained head receipt is required for recovery; old writers are fenced by lock-digest and owner-token checks.
attack_classes.residual_nonclaim: Wall-clock lease semantics are laboratory controls, not Byzantine clock consensus.

attack_classes.threat: A crash after authorization consumption but before executor admission makes the authorization spendable again.
attack_classes.control: Consumption generation is fsync-written and atomically renamed before the controller returns virtual admission; recovered consumed state is non-resumable and uncertain.
attack_classes.residual_nonclaim: The lab proves process-restart ordering, not storage-device power-loss survival.

attack_classes.threat: An authentic older generation set is restored after a newer committed head existed.
attack_classes.control: A separately retained signed durable-head receipt must exactly match the local generation and record digest before a current-head claim is accepted.
attack_classes.residual_nonclaim: Without external retention, local history alone cannot prove a later suffix never existed.

attack_classes.threat: A crash leaves a partially written committed state that is interpreted as valid.
attack_classes.control: Writes go to unique temporary files, are fsynced, then atomically renamed; abandoned temp files are never committed generations.
attack_classes.residual_nonclaim: Atomic rename and fsync semantics depend on the local filesystem and do not establish independent replication.

attack_classes.threat: Missing, duplicated, or conflicting generations hide state transitions.
attack_classes.control: Startup requires exactly one contiguous generation sequence and exact predecessor-record digest chaining.
attack_classes.residual_nonclaim: This is a single-writer local chain, not multi-node agreement.

attack_classes.threat: Lifecycle or receipt payloads are modified on disk.
attack_classes.control: Every record is canonical, Ed25519-signed by the store evidence key, digest-named, and re-verifies lifecycle signatures and exact plan bindings on startup.
attack_classes.residual_nonclaim: A compromised store signing key remains a separate key-compromise problem.

attack_classes.threat: A copied state directory is reopened under another store key.
attack_classes.control: Every record and lock binds the store-key fingerprint and verification requires the trusted corresponding public key.
attack_classes.residual_nonclaim: The software key is not claimed to be HSM, TPM, Secure Enclave, or hardware backed.

attack_classes.threat: A durable store rewrites lifecycle evidence under a different lifecycle signer.
attack_classes.control: The lifecycle private/public key fingerprint must equal the dry-run plan lifecycle-key binding and every transcript/receipt is reverified.
attack_classes.residual_nonclaim: Lifecycle signing authenticates evidence; it is not device or production authority.

attack_classes.threat: Untrusted identifiers cause durable state writes outside the dedicated root.
attack_classes.control: The caller supplies an absolute root; store directories are hash-derived from validated IDs and every internal path is checked to remain beneath that root.
attack_classes.residual_nonclaim: A hostile privileged local filesystem is outside the current trust model.

attack_classes.threat: Revoked, expired, interrupted, or completed state is rewritten into issued or consumed state.
attack_classes.control: The durable generation validator enforces the lifecycle transition graph and terminal-state immutability.
attack_classes.residual_nonclaim: No global revocation oracle is claimed.

attack_classes.threat: Durability evidence is presented as task success, real effects, production persistence, currentness, or authority.
attack_classes.control: Record and head-receipt validators hard-code false production/currentness/effect/authority claims; conformance receipts remain virtual-only.
attack_classes.residual_nonclaim: Passing this laboratory is not executor promotion.

promotion_blockers: production database or replicated state service
independent security review of any effect-reachable executor
